name: Elnathan
overview: Elnathan was a male Levite known for his role as a Levite whom Ezra sent to Iddo. His service is noted specifically in the context of the tribe of Levi, emphasizing his priestly heritage and responsibilities within the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Elnathan means 'G-d is given,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with Hebrew naming traditions. This proper name underscores the recognition of divine provision or gift, though it was not directly given by God according to the record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elnathan as a descendant of Levi, affirming his tribal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Elnathan's significance lies in his role as a Levite sent by Ezra to Iddo, highlighting his participation in the restoration efforts of the Israelite community after the exile. His mention underscores the continued importance of Levites in religious and communal leadership during this period, reflecting God's ongoing provision through His chosen tribe.
